evidence: The round-0 classifyMigrationState called partitionBaselineTables, which only checks tableExists per name, so a workspace with every table but issue_events.assignee un-renamed would be stamped v1. Commit 8d760ba replaced it with verifyBaselineShape, which checks columns parsed from 00001_baseline.sql, and added TestOpenRefusesPreConvergedColumnShape.
guidance_note: When an adoption gate replaces a reconciler that handled column adds and renames, derive the gate's expected shape from the same baseline file at column granularity in the original PR, not from a hand-kept table list.

evidence: The package comment said migrations could be `.sql (or .go)`, but the `//go:embed *.sql` pattern and registryMaxVersion scan only .sql. c39e517 rewrote the comment to say only SQL is wired today.
guidance_note: Before you write a package doc that names supported file kinds, check it against the embed glob and the registry scan.

evidence: The comment said the list was "enforced coherent by CI", while sxsk.4 (the canary) had not landed. c39e517 softened it to "kept coherent by convention today", and 8d760ba then deleted the hand-kept list entirely.
guidance_note: Don't describe a planned ticket's enforcement as present tense in a [LAW:one-source-of-truth] comment; a list that can only be kept in sync by convention should be derived instead.

evidence: This is the same table-only adoption gap as F1, raised again at 18:50 against c39e517. That commit only changed the comments in migration_runner.go and embed.go, and the F1 fix (8d760ba, replied 18:56) had not yet been pushed. So the flag is a false positive: the finding is a duplicate of F1, not caused by a fix.
guidance_note: Push the substantive fix for a round together with the cheap comment fixes, so the reviewer doesn't re-raise the open finding against a comment-only commit.

evidence: Both the adoption stamp and the per-migration loop called commitWorkingSetOnce, which skips the transient-manifest retry. The agent itself calls this "a regression" relative to the old reconcile. The callsites came from the original PR; 8d760ba did not touch them, so the flag is a false positive. c3f3410 switched both to commitWorkingSet.
guidance_note: When replacing a legacy startup path, list the failure semantics it had (here, commit retry) and keep each one in the new runner before opening the PR.

evidence: The F1 fix commit 8d760ba added TestOpenRefusesPreConvergedColumnShape. Its comment says "issues missing the topic/item_rank columns", but the fixture runs only `ALTER TABLE issues DROP COLUMN topic`. 261820e corrected the comment.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a test, reread the test's doc comment against its fixture lines before pushing, and especially check examples copied over from the reply text ("topic/item_rank").

evidence: "epics IS NULL, leaves IN the known set" was ambiguous shorthand that the original PR introduced in ranking.go; c3f3410 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive. 261820e reworded it as suggested.

TestOpenRefusesPartialPreGooseSchema came from the original PR and calls OpenForRead. 261820e only changed comments in baseline_schema_test.go and ranking.go, so the flag is a false positive. The test was renamed to TestOpenForReadRefusesPartialPreGooseSchema.
guidance_note: Name a test after the entrypoint it actually calls.

evidence: withGooseHistoryDropped runs Open first, which always creates goose_db_version. A missing table therefore means the precondition is broken, and a loud `DROP TABLE` failure is the right signal. `IF EXISTS` would let a future refactor silently stop exercising the drop. The helper came from the original PR, not 261820e, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Push back on "make the fixture tolerant" suggestions when the strict statement asserts a precondition the test depends on.

evidence: Declining to refuse Open over benign leftover tables is defensible. But the deferral says the sxsk.4 canary will catch extra tables like issue_history, and the canary as built in #135 dumps the schema of a fresh CI workspace against a snapshot. It never inspects an adopted user workspace, so adopted workspaces keep the drift with nothing tracking it. The flag is a false positive: the gate code was rewritten in 8d760ba, but the absence check was never part of any fix.
guidance_note: Before deferring a finding to a planned ticket, check that the ticket's mechanism actually runs on the population the finding is about (adopted user workspaces, not CI fixtures); otherwise file a follow-up such as a drop-legacy migration.

narrative: This PR replaced the schema reconciler with a goose baseline plus adoption. The real defect was a table-only adoption gate (F1), which the reviewer raised twice (F4) because the comment-only commit c39e517 was pushed before the fix. The column-level fix brought in one comment-drift finding (F6) in its new test. The remaining rounds flagged code from the original PR one item at a time: the commit retry regression, a test name, and a wording nit. One pushback (F10) leaned on a canary that cannot see adopted workspaces.
guidance_observations: Pushing comment-only fixes ahead of the substantive fix for the same round produced a duplicate finding and an extra round.
The original PR dropped the legacy reconciler's commit-retry semantics; an inventory of the old path's guarantees would have caught it before review.

evidence: `--path-format=absolute` needs Git 2.31, and a failure is mapped to ErrNotGitRepo, which misleads the operator. In 411f116 the agent dropped the flag and joined a relative result onto filepath.Abs(cwd), which is what the reviewer's fallback did anyway, with no try-then-sniff second path.
guidance_note: Before using a newer CLI flag, check the minimum version it needs and whether the old output can simply be interpreted correctly.

evidence: printWorkspaceIdentity used `%s` for storage_dir and git_common_dir in a space-separated key=value line, so a path under "My Projects" is ambiguous. The function came from the original PR; the named fix 411f116 only touched workspace.go, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Quote free-form path values when rendering key=value diagnostics.

evidence: The F1 fix 411f116 removed `--path-format=absolute`, but the PR description still described that flag as the approach. The agent updated the description.
guidance_note: When a review fix changes the PR's approach, update the PR description in the same push.

narrative: This PR fixed store resolution from subdirectories. The reviewer rightly flagged the Git 2.31 dependency, and the agent replaced the flag with cwd-anchoring, which is simpler than the suggested fallback. That changed approach left the PR description stale (F3), which shared round 1 with a separate quoting nit on original code, so no round was purely fix-caused.
guidance_observations: A different-fix response should include a pass over the PR body, because the description is the first thing a reviewer reads.

evidence: filepath.EvalSymlinks returns an *os.PathError that already names the failing component, so "doesn't include the path" overstates the gap. Naming the full input path with `%q` still adds the context that component lacks, so taking it was fine.

narrative: This was a small canonicalization fix. One error-context nit was taken in a single commit, and the second round came back clean.

evidence: After a top-level Decode, json.Decoder.More peeks at the next byte and returns true for a following value, so `[...] [...]` is rejected and the reviewer's claim fails. The agent backed this with a test program. There is a kernel both sides missed: More returns false when the next byte is `]` or `}`, so input like `[...]]` passes the "trailing data" check silently. The cited law supports the code's intent but is not evidence that the finding is wrong.
guidance_note: When claiming a parse is total, test stray closing delimiters as well as trailing values, or end with `dec.Token()` and require io.EOF instead of relying on More.

narrative: The single finding was a false claim about json.Decoder.More, and the agent refuted it with an empirical test. Its test table covered trailing values but not trailing `]`/`}`, which More also lets through, so the "every byte stream that is not exactly one array" guarantee in the doc comment is slightly overstated.
guidance_observations: Empirical refutations should probe the boundary the code claims to enforce, not only the counterexample the reviewer named.

evidence: The comment said "A blocks B" while SrcID=A, DstID=B encodes "A depends on B" under the src=dependent convention, which the agent confirmed. 983722a corrected the comment and the fatal message, one of the two remedies offered. The packet doesn't show the convention's definition; this rests on both parties' agreement.
guidance_note: When seeding relation edges in tests, write the comment from the store's src/dst convention rather than from intent.

evidence: The sibling test TestMigrateSnapshotRestoreRoundTripsPreMutationState already asserts rotated != "". The new test omitted that assertion, and 983722a added it.
guidance_note: When writing a test modeled on a sibling test, carry over the sibling's invariant assertions.

evidence: `issueC, err := ...; _ = issueC` came from the original commit. 983722a only changed the relation comment and the rotated assertion, so the flag is a false positive.

narrative: This test-only PR had three small, valid nits, all taken. The round-1 finding was on original code that round 0 had not flagged, so no round was caused by a fix.

evidence: applyPendingMigrations got state.appliedVersion=0 on phaseAdopt even though adoption had just stamped v1, so a v1 quarantine row would block. cb874c9 set state.appliedVersion = baselineVersion and moved the test to a v2 row. That assignment became dead once the F6 fix moved the gate (see F14).
guidance_note: After a step mutates persisted state, recompute the derived value at the point of use instead of patching an in-memory copy that other code may stop reading.

evidence: With retain < 0, the slice `cps[:len(cps)-retain]` goes out of bounds and panics. cb874c9 returns an error for negative retain at entry.
guidance_note: For an exported helper that takes a count, reject illegal ranges at entry when writing it.

evidence: handleMigrationFailure leaves version=0 when result or result.Source is nil, and Error() then printed `DELETE ... WHERE version = 0`. cb874c9 added a Version==0 branch. That branch shipped untested (F13) and with a placeholder `lit snapshots restore <name>` (F19).
guidance_note: When adding an error-message branch, add the test that forces it in the same commit, and check the wording against the wrapper the error is always returned inside.

evidence: The TestMigrationFailureCheckpointPath doc comment said the next Open returns QuarantineBlockError, while the test expects success. That comment came from the original PR, and cb874c9 did not touch this test, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Before opening the PR, check each new test's doc comment against what the test asserts.

evidence: The reviewer said time.Unix reconstructs in UTC, but time.Unix returns Local, exactly like time.Now. The agent's own reply says so ("time.Unix(0, ns) returns local time; time.Now() also returns local time") and then applied the change anyway. CreateCheckpoint came from the original PR; cb874c9 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When your own analysis refutes a finding's premise, push back instead of applying the suggestion to close the thread.

evidence: In the original PR, checkPendingQuarantine ran inside applyPendingMigrations after guard.ensure() had taken a snapshot, so every blocked Open added a snapshot. cb874c9 did not change this, so the flag is a false positive. c73db91 moved the check into quarantineFastFail before the guard. That move left the state param unused (F9), a stale test comment (F12) and a dead appliedVersion store (F14).
guidance_note: When moving a check to an earlier stage, grep for every input that existed only to feed it (params, state mutations, comments, test docs) and delete or update them in the same commit.

evidence: The column was `version INT NOT NULL` while goose versions are int64, and timestamp-style goose versions exceed 2^31. The DDL came from the original PR, not cb874c9, so the flag is a false positive. c73db91 changed it to BIGINT.
guidance_note: Match each SQL column type to the Go type it stores when writing the DDL.

evidence: CreateCheckpoint, ResetToCheckpoint and PruneCheckpoints are exported and documented as reusable, yet they mutate Dolt HEAD/branches outside withCommitLock. Every other commit boundary takes that lock, and it short-circuits when already held (#129). The agent applied a null-guard law "in spirit" to a mutation-boundary invariant. A no-cost wrap, or unexporting the methods and dropping the reusability claim, would remove the gap. The methods came from the original PR; c73db91 only changed a timestamp to UTC, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When adding exported methods that mutate the same resource as an existing lock-guarded boundary, route them through that boundary or keep them unexported; don't publish an unguarded reusable API.

evidence: c73db91 (the F6 fix) deleted the only use of `state` in applyPendingMigrations, the checkPendingQuarantine call, but kept the parameter. 4f40a15 removed it.
guidance_note: After removing a call from a function, check whether each parameter is still read.

evidence: CreateCheckpoint ran before newGooseProvider, so a provider failure would leave an unpruned branch. This ordering came from the original PR; c73db91 only changed surrounding comments. 4f40a15 swapped the order.
guidance_note: Acquire resources that need cleanup (branches, snapshots) after the fallible pure setup.

evidence: `before, _ := st.ListCheckpoints(...)` in the original test discarded the error. c73db91 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Don't discard errors in tests either.

evidence: c73db91 (the F6 fix) added an assertion that QuarantineBlockError is NOT wrapped in MigrationRollbackError. The test's doc comment above still said "(inside MigrationRollbackError)" and "appliedVersion=0", which the F1 fix had already made wrong. f116b17 rewrote it.
guidance_note: When a fix adds an assertion that inverts a test's contract, rewrite that test's doc comment in the same commit.

evidence: cb874c9 (the F3 fix) added the Version==0 branch of CheckpointResetError.Error with no test. f116b17 added TestCheckpointResetErrorUnknownVersion, which forces a nil result through migrationUpByOneForTest.
guidance_note: A fix that adds a branch ships with the test that reaches it; the injection hook already existed.

evidence: The F1 fix had added `state.appliedVersion = baselineVersion` with a comment saying it fed checkPendingQuarantine. The F6 fix (c73db91) moved that check into quarantineFastFail, which handles phaseAdopt itself, and 4f40a15 dropped the param, leaving a dead store plus a false comment. b0d35c3 removed both.
guidance_note: When relocating logic that an earlier review fix patched, search for that earlier patch and decide its fate in the same commit.

evidence: In the original PR, PruneCheckpoints ran only on ErrNoNextVersion, so nil-result failures, which write no quarantine row, accumulated branches. b0d35c3 only removed the dead store, so the flag is a false positive. Accepting was right, but the fix in 98e2f3e swallows the prune error with `_ =` instead of joining it to the returned error.
guidance_note: Put retention on every exit path (defer) when the resource is created; when adding a secondary cleanup on an error path, join its error (errors.Join) rather than discarding it.

evidence: Nanosecond-name collisions need two CreateCheckpoint calls in the same clock tick. Production makes one per Open, under the commit lock, so a retry loop would be complexity for a synthetic loop only the tests produce. The naming came from the original PR, and b0d35c3 did not touch checkpoint.go, so the flag is a false positive.

recordQuarantine wrote RFC3339 while the rest of the store persists RFC3339Nano. The code came from the original PR, and 98e2f3e only added the failure-path prune, so the flag is a false positive. The mismatch is a consistency issue, not two authorities for one fact, so one-source-of-truth is a stretch.
guidance_note: When persisting a timestamp, reuse the store's existing format helper rather than choosing a format locally.

evidence: It is true that a quarantine row above registryMax blocks Open. Blocking on an uncleared quarantine after a downgrade is a defensible conservative choice, though the agent's second reason (it would need a real v2 migration for the test) is a test-convenience argument. The unbounded `version > ?` query came from the original PR, and 33848e7 only changed the timestamp format, so the flag is a false positive.

F3 was about a misleading operator instruction when Version==0. Its fix (cb874c9) replaced the instruction with another one, the placeholder `lit snapshots restore <name>`, inside an error always wrapped by MigrationRollbackError, which prints the real snapshot name. The inner copy was a second, fake recovery instruction.
guidance_note: When fixing an error message, read it as the operator will see it, nested inside its wrapper, before pushing.

evidence: The original test file hand-rolled contains/containsAt instead of using strings.Contains; 33848e7 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Use the stdlib helper instead of reimplementing it in tests.

evidence: The three handleMigrationFailure error paths (reset, insert, commit) omitted checkpoint.Name, the one forensics anchor available. That code came from the original PR, and 33848e7 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Every failure-path error in a recovery routine should name the recovery artifact it was working with.

narrative: The checkpoint and quarantine PR took ten rounds. Most findings were on original code that the reviewer surfaced a few per round. The F6 fix (moving the quarantine gate before the snapshot) left three leftovers: an unused param (F9), a stale test comment (F12) and a dead store from the F1 fix (F14). Round 3 (F12, F13) and round 4 (F14) consisted only of fix-caused findings. The F3 fix needed two follow-ups: a missing test (F13) and a placeholder instruction (F19). The agent applied one premise it had itself refuted (F5), and declined the commit-lock finding (F8) on a misapplied law.
guidance_observations: A gate relocation should end with a sweep for every artifact the old location needed (params, in-memory patches, comments); here three rounds of findings came from skipping that sweep.
Adding a test in the same commit as each new error-message branch would have removed F13, and reading the message inside its wrapper would have removed F19.
Several pushbacks and accepts were decided in under two minutes; F5 shows an accept despite the agent's own correct refutation.

evidence: `out, _ := difflib.GetUnifiedDiffString(...)` discarded the error, so a diff failure would show an empty drift report. 1ca9893 surfaces the error together with both documents.
guidance_note: Don't discard errors from diagnostic helpers; the diagnostic is the thing being protected.

evidence: The table names come from information_schema in a test-created database, so "SQL-injection-style" overstates the risk. Still, doubling backticks is the canonical way to quote an identifier that can't be bound, and the change is one line.
guidance_note: Escape interpolated identifiers by default, even in test code.

narrative: The schema-drift canary drew two small valid findings, both fixed in one commit. Two clean rounds followed. The canary compares a freshly converged CI workspace against the snapshot, so it does not cover the adopted-workspace drift #129/F10 deferred to it.

evidence: The stampGooseVersionAhead comment said the stamp is observed "from the checkpoint state", but the helper only commits the working set. It was reworded to "from the committed working set".
guidance_note: Avoid reusing domain terms (checkpoint) loosely in comments once they name a concrete mechanism.

narrative: The workspace-ahead-of-binary refusal drew one terminology nit on a test helper comment, which was fixed, and the next round was clean.
